# Permanently expired offline-verifier fixture

This bundle is byte-identical to `../attested/bundle` except for its RFC 3161 sidecar, which
carries a token signed by `tsa-root.pem` — a test timestamp authority whose validity window is

    notBefore = Jan  1 00:00:00 2015 GMT
    notAfter  = Jan  1 00:00:00 2016 GMT

and can never reopen. Its expected verdict is **`EXPIRED` (exit 4) with the record chain, the
receipt signatures and the anchor signature still verifying**, and that is what
`tests/fixtures/conformance/expired-tsa` pins and CI runs.

**Do not regenerate this fixture with current dates.** R-008 F-10 was a twenty-four-hour
certificate in the one CI job that demonstrates what Mizan is for: it could never have passed on
any day but the day it was generated, and nobody knew because the job had never run. The defect
underneath was the verifier, not the certificate, and moving a fixture's dates forward is how that
defect would have gone back into hiding. If this fixture goes red, either the verifier stopped
distinguishing `EXPIRED` from `FAIL` or it stopped verifying the rest of the bundle past the
horizon. Both are the thing this fixture exists to catch.

Regenerated by `scripts/build_tsa_fixtures.py`, which needs OpenSSL 3.5 or newer. Verification
needs any OpenSSL 3.x.

Note what the token shows about the naive repair: its `genTime` is 2026, well outside its signer's
validity window, because nothing in RFC 3161 ties the two together. Dating a certificate by the
token it signed proves nothing, which is why the verifier re-checks at an instant taken from the
certificates instead.
